transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because my sleep has become a real issue lately. I’m usually a very disciplined sleeper, but since my cousin died, I just lie awake replaying that night. And then if I do manage to drift off, I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning from these... scraps of hospital images in my head. I end up going into board meetings feeling like I’ve only slept in pieces, and I just can't keep functioning like that.
When you’re awake, do you find yourself having sudden, intrusive memories or flashbacks of the night your cousin passed away?

Yes, I do. It usually happens at odd moments. For example, if a phone rings late, or... if I catch the glare of headlights on the highway, a really sharp picture of the hospital corridor will just push right into my mind. Or I'll suddenly hear the police officer’s voice again. 

It's very abrupt. When it happens, I usually just have to pause for a second and take a breath to steady myself before I can get back to whatever I was doing.
Since your cousin’s passing, have you noticed yourself avoiding certain places, people, or situations that remind you of what happened?

No, not really. I mean, I still drive the same routes to work, and I still talk to my family about... well, about normal things. I haven't stopped going anywhere or seeing anyone. I just try to keep my routine as normal as possible.
Since your cousin passed away, have you noticed any changes in your mood or thoughts—like feeling more irritable, detached, or struggling with negative beliefs about yourself or the world?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel detached, and my beliefs are pretty much the same. But... I have noticed I'm a lot more irritable. 

I've actually snapped at my leadership team a few times recently. It's over really small things, like minor delays or just the wording in an email. I've used a tone with them that, honestly, I would normally consider completely unacceptable for a CEO. And then... I just feel embarrassed afterward, because I know they haven't really done anything wrong. It's just my own frustration spilling over.
Since your cousin’s passing, have you found yourself being more on edge, easily startled, or unusually watchful, like you’re constantly alert for danger?

Yes, I have noticed that. Mostly when I'm driving. 

I find myself constantly checking the mirrors, watching the speed of any trucks around me, looking for places I could pull off if I had to. Even when I'm just taking the familiar roads to the office, my body stays completely tight. It's like I'm just waiting for something bad to happen.
Since your cousin passed away, have you had days where you feel down or lose interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a little while?

Well, I don't know if I'd call it feeling down exactly, but... I have noticed a shift in how I experience things. 

Like, during the prayer gatherings we had for him, and even when my nieces came over and tried to comfort me... I just didn't feel anything positive. I was going through the motions, behaving properly, saying the right things, but there was no warmth or relief inside me. It's almost as if the affectionate part of me has just gone quiet. I just feel kind of empty in those moments when I know I should be feeling some sort of connection or comfort.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms? Have they been going on for more than a month now?
No, it hasn't been a month yet. It's been going on for about three weeks now... ever since the night he died in that highway collision.
Have these symptoms been affecting your ability to function normally in your daily life, such as at work, in relationships, or in taking care of yourself?

Yes, it has been affecting things. I'm still showing up for the most essential meetings at the office, but... I've had to delegate a lot of my community obligations. I've also been shortening my workdays. I'm just not as steady or effective with people as I normally am right now, so I'm pulling back where I can.

Do you think your symptoms are mainly a result of the trauma from witnessing or experiencing the events around your cousin’s death, or do you feel like they’re more related to the general stress and sadness of losing him?

I'm not really sure how to separate the two, to be honest. I mean, losing him is incredibly sad, obviously... but the suddenness of it, the highway collision, it all just kind of blends together in my head. 

I don't know if it's the shock of how it happened or just the general grief of him being gone. I haven't really been able to parse that out. It just feels like one heavy thing right now.
Have you noticed that you’re unable to feel positive emotions like happiness, satisfaction, or love since your cousin passed away?

Yes, I have noticed that. It's actually been quite noticeable to me. During the prayer gatherings for him, and... even when my nieces tried to comfort me recently, I just felt kind of empty. I found myself behaving properly, saying the right things, but I felt no warmth or relief inside. It's almost as if the affectionate part of me has just gone completely quiet. I don't feel any of those positive things right now.
Have you found yourself experiencing strong feelings of anger, guilt, or blame related to the events around your cousin’s death?

No, not really. I mean, I'm terribly sad, but I don't feel angry about it. And I don't feel guilty or blame anyone, either. It was a tragic accident, but I don't have those kinds of strong, angry feelings about it.
Have you noticed that you feel consistently down or emotionally numb since your cousin passed away, like the sadness or emptiness never really lifts?

Well, I wouldn't say it's constant. I mean, I definitely feel that emptiness we just talked about, where I can't seem to feel the good things... but it's not like I'm walking around feeling a heavy, crushing sadness every single second of the day. There are moments where I just feel... neutral, I guess? Or just focused on getting through whatever task is in front of me. So no, it doesn't feel like a constant, never-lifting thing.
Have you found yourself trying not to talk about or think about the events surrounding your cousin’s death, or do you find those thoughts coming up regardless of what you’re doing?

No, I haven't really been trying to avoid it. I mean, it's a terrible thing that happened, but I don't find myself actively trying to push thoughts of it away or avoiding talking about it. The thoughts do come up, of course, but not in a way where they're constantly intruding on whatever I'm doing. It's just... I think about it sometimes, but I'm not running from it, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you feel little interest or pleasure in doing things you usually enjoy, even when you're not thinking about your cousin?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in things. I mean, I still enjoy reading in the evenings, and I still like going for my morning walks. It's not like I've stopped caring about the things I usually like to do. I just... I might not feel quite as enthusiastic as I did before, but the interest is definitely still there.
Have you found that the emptiness or sadness you’re feeling tends to stay with you most of the day, nearly every day, even if it’s not extremely intense?

No, I really don't think it's like that. I mean, I don't feel sad or empty most of the day, or every day for that matter. Like I said, I have moments where I feel that emptiness, but it's definitely not a constant thing that just hangs over me all day long. Most of the time, I'm just going about my normal routine.
